sso.intro: Applications that sign users in with their domain account through conductor-idp (OpenID Connect and SAML 2.0).
sso.disabled.title: Single sign-on is not enabled
sso.disabled.text: Install conductor-idp, enable its management API ([api] in idp.toml and conductor-idp-api.socket) and set [idp] enabled = true in conductor.toml.
sso.directory_down: conductor-idp cannot read the directory with its service account: sign-ins fail until it can.

sso.keys.next_oidc: Next scheduled OpenID Connect key rotation: {0}.
sso.new.title: Add an application
sso.new.intro: Pick a guided preset or start from a generic one. Every preset only fills the form: you choose who may sign in and review everything before it is saved.
sso.new.import_hint: Any SAML application that publishes metadata: import it by URL, file or text.
sso.preset.google-workspace.hint: Users sign in to Google with their domain account (SAML). Needs a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization; the users must exist in Google with the same e-mail (as conductor-sync creates them).
sso.preset.google-workspace.after: Then, in Google's Admin console (Security, Authentication, SSO with third party IdP), create a SAML profile with the values shown on this application's page and assign it to an organizational unit.
sso.preset.grafana.hint: Grafana's generic OAuth with PKCE, roles from group names.
sso.preset.grafana.after: In grafana.ini [auth.generic_oauth]: client_id and client_secret from the next page, use_pkce = true, scopes = openid profile email groups, the issuer's discovery for the URLs, and role_attribute_path on groups.
sso.preset.nextcloud.hint: Nextcloud's OpenID Connect user backend (user_oidc app).
sso.preset.nextcloud.after: In Nextcloud, OpenID Connect settings: the client_id and secret from the next page, the issuer's discovery URL, and PKCE on.
sso.preset.gitlab.after: In gitlab.rb, an openid_connect provider with the issuer, discovery: true, pkce: true and the client_id and secret from the next page.
sso.preset.generic-oidc.hint: Any OpenID Connect application (authorization code with PKCE).
sso.preset.generic-saml.hint: Any SAML 2.0 service provider, configured by hand (or import its metadata instead).
sso.preset.generic-saml.after: Fill in the entity ID and the ACS URL from the application's documentation.
sso.preset.param.domain_hint: The domain of the users' e-mail addresses in Google.
sso.preset.param.entity_id_hint: New SAML profiles in Google's Admin console show their own entity ID (accounts.google.com/samlrp/...): paste it. Empty: the legacy google.com/a/<domain>.
sso.preset.param.acs_url_hint: From the same profile page. Empty: the legacy https://www.google.com/a/<domain>/acs.
sso.preset.param.base_url_hint: https, as users open it (with a path when it is not at the root).
sso.preset.param.redirect_uri_hint: The callback the application documents; it must match exactly.

sso.google.hint: Security, Authentication, SSO with third party IdP: add a SAML profile with these values, then assign it to the organizational units that should use it.
sso.keys.intro: OpenID Connect keys rotate every {0} days; a replaced key stays published {1} hours. SAML keys rotate in stages, because applications pin the certificate.
sso.keys.saml_staged_long: A SAML rotation is staged: the new certificate is in the metadata now and signs from {0}. Give it to every SAML application (Google Workspace takes one certificate at a time) before then.

sso.keys.rotate_saml_warning: Give the new certificate to every SAML application before the switch.

import.title: Import from Google Workspace
import.intro: For a company that already uses Google Workspace and starts its AD now: create in AD, once, the users (and optionally the groups) that exist in Google. conductor-sync only reads Google; conductor creates the AD objects with your account after a full preview. Passwords cannot be imported: each new user gets a random password nobody knows and must change it at next sign-in, and you set an initial password when onboarding the person (Reset password). Each new account's e-mail is its Google address, so the sync then adopts the existing Google account instead of creating one. Nothing is deleted and nothing is written to Google.

import.sub_org_units: Include the org units below them

import.member_of_hint: Group addresses, one per line (nested membership counts). Empty: no group filter.

import.fallback_hint: The logon name is the part of the address before @ when it is valid (at most 20 characters, no " / \ [ ] : ; | = , + * ? < > @) and free. Otherwise this template: {given}, {family}, {g} (first letter of the given name), {f}, {local}; accents are removed. A name that is still taken is reported, not invented.

import.accounts_hint: Enabled is as safe as disabled while nobody knows the password, and the sync adopts the Google account at once. A disabled AD user never adopts its Google account (the sync reports disabled-not-adopted) until you enable it.

accounts.title: Connected accounts
accounts.intro: Your accounts in other services that the organization provisions from this directory. You can activate yours and set a new password here. Passwords are never stored by conductor.
accounts.mfa_needed: Turn on two-step verification to activate an account or set a password here.
accounts.activate_hint: Creates your {0} account now. You get its password once, on the next page.
accounts.reset_hint: Sets a new password on your {0} account. Your current password there stops working.

branding.title: Branding
branding.intro: The look of the pages users see: the self-service portal here and the sign-in pages of the single sign-on provider. Administration pages keep the product look.
branding.problems_files: Choose the new images again: uploads of a refused form are not kept.
branding.push: Send to the sign-in pages again
branding.hint.org_name: Shown in the header and the page titles instead of the product name.
branding.hint.primary_color: #rrggbb. Buttons, links and the current menu entry. It must reach a contrast of 4.5:1 on a light background (WCAG AA); the dark theme uses a lighter shade automatically.
branding.hint.accent_color: #rrggbb. The line under the header and the notice banner; text on it is chosen automatically.
branding.hint.images: Checked by their content and served from this site. SVG is not accepted.
branding.hint.help: Shown under the sign-in form and on the self-service home page.
branding.hint.notice: Shown at the top of every branded page, for example a maintenance window. Leave empty to hide it.
branding.hint.consent: Shown on the single sign-on consent page; it is part of the single sign-on settings.
branding.hint.links: https addresses, or mailto: and tel: links.
branding.problem.contrast: contrast {0}:1 on a light background; at least 4.5:1 is needed for links and buttons (choose a darker color)
branding.problem.accent_contrast: contrast {0}:1 against the header; below 3:1 the line is hard to see
branding.problem.url: must be an https address, or a mailto: or tel: link
branding.problem.phone: use digits, spaces, parentheses, dots, hyphens and a leading +
branding.problem.asset: the image description is not valid
branding.problem.svg_refused: SVG images are not accepted (they can carry scripts); use PNG, JPEG or WebP
branding.problem.image_dimensions: larger than {0} pixels on a side
branding.problem.image_corrupt: the image could not be read
branding.preview.title: Branding preview
branding.preview.intro: How the sign-in and self-service pages will look, in the light and the dark theme. Nothing is saved yet. Switch the language in the footer to check the other texts.
branding.preview.stale: The branding changed since this edit started. Saving it will be refused: edit again from the current version.
branding.save.title: Save the branding
branding.save.summary: The branding becomes a new version, shown at once on the self-service and sign-in pages.
branding.err.image_missing: An image of this branding is missing; choose it again.
branding.err.stale: The branding changed since this edit started; nothing was saved. Edit again from the current version.
branding.err.push: Saved, but the sign-in pages were not updated: {0}
branding.err.push_failed: The sign-in pages were not updated.
branding.err.idp_too_old: The single sign-on provider is older and does not support branding; upgrade it.
branding.err.version_invalid: That version is not valid anymore and cannot be restored.
branding.push.title: Send the branding to the sign-in pages
branding.push.summary: The single sign-on provider receives version {0} again.
branding.revert.title: Restore a branding version
branding.revert.summary: Version {0} becomes the current branding again, as a new version.
branding.revert.summary_reset: The pages go back to the product look, as a new version.
branding.versions.intro: Every save and every restore is a new version; the newest {0} are kept.
branding.versions.none: The branding was never saved: the pages have the product look.
branding.versions.reset_hint: Removes the organization name, colors, images and texts, as a new version that can itself be undone.
